  others: in=[i]     out=[o]    linear -- 1->1    (pass-through in any order)

EDGE ROUTING INSIDE A FSPLIT/FFUSE PAIR
  FSPLIT.T -> [tokens, anchored by EVALT (primary) or AFWD (secondary)] -> FFUSE.T
  FSPLIT.F -> [tokens, anchored by EVALF (primary) or AREV (secondary)] -> FFUSE.F
  If T-arm empty: FSPLIT.T connects directly to FFUSE.T (empty arc, T-state)
  If F-arm empty: FSPLIT.F connects directly to FFUSE.F (empty arc, F-state)
  The first immediate EVALT/EVALF anchors select arm segments. Later operations
  in a selected segment remain on that arm, including repeated evaluators.
  Without a primary anchor, AREV selects the F-arm and AFWD the T-arm.
    With primary anchors, intervening operations stay in their selected arm.
    Secondary anchors activate only when the primary (EVALT/EVALF) anchor is absent.
  Nesting: FSPLIT/FFUSE pairs may nest; innermost pairs matched first

BANKING A RESULT BEFORE REVERSING IT
  AREV empties the register and leaves open FSPLIT frames untouched. A result
  fused back to depth zero is therefore exposed to the next reversal, while the
  same result held one level up survives it.
  So when a program COUNTS or ESTABLISHES something, then REVERSES direction
  (AREV), then BOUNDS or CONCLUDES: open the region that will HOLD the result
  BEFORE opening the region that COMPUTES it, and close them in that order.
    wrong: ... FSPLIT compute FFUSE  CLINK  FSPLIT AREV bound FFUSE ...
             the computed result is in the open when AREV arrives and is lost
    right: ... FSPLIT  FSPLIT compute FFUSE  CLINK AREV bound  FFUSE ...
             the inner FFUSE folds into the enclosing frame, AREV costs the
             register everything and the frame nothing, the outer FFUSE
             restores exactly what the clear took
  This is what a proof does when it establishes a lemma and keeps it in scope
  while a later chain runs: the lemma is the outer frame.

  A SECOND AND INDEPENDENT RULE. Whether anything is banked is the above.
  Whether a SURPLUS survives is a different question, decided by where the
  splits fall between deposits of the SAME value:
    two EVALT in ONE region      -> the region carries both, both come back
    two EVALT split by an FSPLIT -> sibling regions, the fold keeps the LARGER
  So a program can bank correctly and still lose a count, and a program can
  deposit carefully into one region and lose everything because its FFUSE ran
  before the reversal. Neither rule implies the other; both are proved in
  p4ramill Imscribing/IMASM/BankedWeight.lean.
  Explicit graph tools support cross-branch routing. This JSON schema carries
  a sequence only; imscr_wiring supplies its standard edges. It does not
  accept arbitrary cross-branch overrides.

EXPLICIT GRAPH COMPOSITION
  CLINK.o, IMSCRIB.o and IFIX.o may connect to compatible free inputs.
  A connection does not assign a register value by itself. The graph-flow
  evaluator computes that value from source seeds and the executed gates.
  This sequence-only schema cannot request arbitrary loop edges.

REGISTER STATE TRANSITIONS
  Sequential banked evaluator, carrier P({T,F,t,f}):
  VINIT clears register and frames. TANCH and CLINK preserve state.
  AFWD and IMSCRIB seed T only when the register is empty.
  AREV clears the register and retains open frames.
  EVALT deposits T; EVALF deposits F; ENGAGR deposits both t and f.
  FSPLIT opens an empty frame; FFUSE unions its deposits into the register
  and enclosing frame. IFIX freezes subsequent operations except IMSCRIB
  and repeated IFIX. Repeated IFIX does not create another mutable state.
  The graph-flow interpreter is a separate interpretation of explicit edges:
  AREV is the Lean involution, EVALT/EVALF are projections and IFIX carries.
  Diagram node observations of the sequential walk are not graph edge flow.

FREE COMPOSITION RULES
  1. Use as many tokens as the domain requires -- there is NO minimum or maximum length
  2. Expand token by token until every distinct operation, branch, state,
     and decision in the domain has been explicitly represented
  3. Each step: "OPCODE: what this token does at this point in the composition"
  4. Every FSPLIT must have exactly one matching FFUSE (stack-matched, innermost first).
     That stack rule is the WIRING convention: it says which arms get routed to which
     join when the sequence is built. It is NOT how closure is judged. A checker pairs
     by ANCESTRY over the edges -- two distinct in-arms of a FFUSE tracing back to a
     common FSPLIT, however they routed -- and where several FSPLIT qualify (an upstream
     fork reaches every later join on a strand) the join pairs with the INNERMOST one.
     The two agree on a plain strand, which is why the stack rule is a sound way to
     WRITE a sequence; they part company as soon as edges route otherwise (cross-branch,
     rule 6 below).
  5. EVALT anchors the T-branch; EVALF anchors the F-branch.
     AFWD (forward morphism) also anchors T-branch if EVALT is absent.
     AREV (parity flip / reverse morphism) also anchors F-branch if EVALF is absent.
  6. ENGAGR at any position enters B-state (paradice: both simultaneously held)
  7. IMSCRIB at both first and last position creates a self-referential closed loop
  8. Multiple FSPLIT/FFUSE pairs (sequential or nested) map multiple branch points
  9. Use IFIX as many times as needed -- each is a distinct permanent record event
  10. Do NOT compress -- if the domain has 30 distinct operations, write 30 tokens

WHY RULE 2 AND RULE 10 ARE SAFE (inflation invariance)
  Expanding costs nothing structural. A 1->1 token adds exactly one node and one edge,
  so the circuit rank beta = E - V + C cannot move, and the census (branch, merge,
  source, sink, arms) cannot move either. Extent grows without bound; structure does
  not. This is why "expand token by token" and "do NOT compress" are free instructions
  rather than a distortion of the domain: a longer faithful sequence is the SAME
  topology as a shorter one, never a different one.
  IMSCRIB (⊙) is the neutral element of that expansion: it is identity/self-reference
  and does NOT transform, so inserting it at any depth leaves the verdict untouched.
  The transforming tokens (> < ⋈ ⊤ ⊥ ⊞ ⊡) are NOT neutral -- a single one placed on an
  arm between FSPLIT and FFUSE turns an identity closure into a real one. So: expand
  freely to map the domain, but only put a transforming token on an arm when the domain
  really does work there.
  A token is irreducible in KIND but unbounded in EXTENT: any 1->2 replacement must
  itself contain a FSPLIT (it is the only brancher), so a fork reappears inside its own
  expansion. Same for FFUSE (2->1) and VINIT (0->1).


TOPOLOGICAL DIVERSITY
=====================
The IMASM composition rules explicitly permit nesting, open forks, and cross-branch routing.
DO NOT default to flat chains when the domain requires richer topology.

NESTING: FSPLIT/FFUSE pairs may nest. A branch can itself contain a sub-fork:
  FSPLIT EVALT [inner FSPLIT EVALT EVALF FFUSE] EVALF FFUSE
Use when the domain has hierarchical sub-decisions within a branch.

OPEN FORKS: A FSPLIT without a matching FFUSE creates a permanently divergent path.
Its unmatched output ports remain open; a later VINIT is a separate source.
Use when the domain has independent parallel processes that never recombine.

CROSS-BRANCH: arbitrary cross-branch edges require the explicit graph tools.
This sequence-only output schema uses imscr_wiring standard routing; do not claim
that prose descriptions add or override its edges.

EMPTY BRANCHES: FSPLIT immediately followed by FFUSE is valid (vacuous evaluation).
Use when the structural form matters more than a particular branch's content.

DECISION VS ITERATION: FSPLIT models a genuine either/or, two arms that could each be
taken because the domain actually forks on a choice. Building n similar items in
sequence (n cliques, n rounds of one process, n members of a family) is not a decision
and takes a CLINK chain, one CLINK per item, never an FSPLIT, even when n is a variable
and even when there are many of them. A fork earns its FFUSE by putting genuinely
different content on each arm. An empty arm is permitted. Structural closure needs a transformed reconnection.
The insert-repair banked-clear observation asks whether a clear had protected
weight; its vacuity result does not decide graph reconnection or arm work.

Choose the topology that best fits the domain. Flat chains are ONE option, not the default.

# Horn Torus Geometry — Context Sheet

Source: `manuscripts3/sic_moduli_conductor.tex`, section "The Geometric
Realization: The Horn Torus and (16,3) Knot," plus the cross-reference against
`millennium_theorems_as_ovms.txt` worked out 2026-08-23.

## The object

A horn torus is the degenerate torus where tube radius equals centre radius,
R = r. The hole closes to a single point instead of staying open. That point
is the pinch, marked ⊙. It is not a drawing artifact — it is the condition
that lets the surface touch itself, the geometric picture of self-reference.

Two lobes, each of radius R, centred at x = ±R on the syzygy axis, tangent at
the origin. The tangency point is ⊙.

## The named features and their coordinates

Side-on section (xz-plane, y=0), the frame the paper actually draws in:

- **⊙ (pinch).** Origin. Where the two lobes touch.
- **λ_C (the split shell).** Dashed circle centred on ⊙, radius r = R/2. This
  is the ∈ split — the completeness coordinate given a located geometric
  home.
- **Evaluator sphere.** Same radius r as λ_C, centred one radius along the
  axis from ⊙. Passes through both ⊙ and ∋.
- **∋.** At x = 2. The far point the evaluator sphere reaches.
- **Coupler.** The heavy segment between ⊙ and ∋ — the line the evaluator
  sphere's passage traces out.
- **Evaluator trine.** ⊤, ⊥, ⊞ at x = 1, z = 0, ±√3/2 in this section —
  collinear here because the section is edge-on to it. In the axial view
  (looking down the syzygy axis) the trine is face-on: an equilateral
  triangle at 120° on a circle. Exact coordinates, confirmed against
  `WINDING/massive_winding/winding_reformulation/k3v_geometry/evaluator_sphere/evaluator_sphere_analysis.md`:
  EVALT (λ_C, λ_C, 0), EVALF (λ_C, −λ_C/2, λ_C√3/2), ENGAGR ⊞ (λ_C, −λ_C/2,
  −λ_C√3/2) — all three on the evaluator sphere's equatorial circle at
  x = λ_C, by construction. **ENGAGR (⊞) also sits on the horn torus surface
  itself** — not in the same untilted frame the evaluator sphere is drawn
  in, but under the tilt that reconciles the two: the evaluator frame (3
  arms on the Compton/evaluator sphere) and the 16-sector grid (the (16,3)
  knot on the horn torus) are related by a rotation of arctan(1/4) around
  the syzygy axis, a 7.5° sector offset (`k3v_geometry/parametric_arm/parametric_arm_analysis.md`
  §5.2). A same-frame membership check against the untilted torus equation
  will show ENGAGR off the surface — that checks the wrong frame, not the
  wrong claim.
- **γ(0), outer equator.** Marker at x = 2R.
- **γ(π), the horn.** The pinch itself, where the equatorial curve
  degenerates — same point as ⊙, named from the curve's parametrization
  rather than the tangency.

Top-down section (z=0): the same λ_C and evaluator-sphere circles side by
side, ∋ at x=2, and the three 120°-equator points are the A₂ roots (one n₊
against two n₋) — their triangle is the knot's poloidal winding read as a
circuit. This equatorial A₂ triangle is **not** the evaluator trine; the
trine collapses to the short edge-on segment at x=1 in this view. Two
different triangles, both real, do not conflate them.

Axial section (looking down the syzygy axis): the outline is unchanged
(horn is symmetric about this axis), but ⊙, the coupler, and ∋, which were
spread out in the other two views, now stack on the axis with ⊙ nearest.
λ_C and the evaluator sphere become one circle (concentric, equal radius).
The trine, edge-on everywhere else, is face-on here — this is the view
where ⊤, ⊥, ⊞ actually show as the equilateral triangle at 120°.

## The (16,3) knot

Sixteen toroidal windings against three poloidal ones, traced by the
evaluator arms. Bridge number three matches the three arms carrying the
four-valued kernel. Sixteen matches the trilattice's state count (2⁴ = 16,
also |I|² = 16 — the two coincide only at n=4, Proposition 2.3 in the
paper). This pair (16,3) is also the conductor exponent structure at
d=2048: 𝔣 = (2¹²)∞₁ = (16³)∞₁.

## Mark-to-feature table

| Feature | Mark(s) | Named role |
|---|---|---|
| Pinch ⊙ | ⊙ (criticality) | Tangency; hole closes to a point |
| Split shell λ_C | ∈ (completeness) | Radius r = R/2, centred on the pinch |
| Evaluator sphere / coupler / ∋ | ∋ (composition) | Passes through ⊙ and ∋, radius r |
| Trine, vertex 1 | ⊤ (dynamics) | Static for all seven Clay theorems alike — not a differentiator |
| Trine, vertex 2 | ⊥ (chirality) | "Return in exactly two steps" |
| Trine, vertex 3 | ⊞ (self-reference) | μ∘δ = id closure; on the evaluator sphere AND the horn torus surface (via the arctan(1/4) tilt) — the only trine member confirmed on both |
| Knot winding overall | ⊡ (winding) | Not a point — the toroidal count itself, 16 turns |
| Involution / parity | ≺ | Not pictured as a torus feature in this paper |

## Cross-reference to the seven Clay theorems

Reading each theorem's OVM-coordinate word (`millennium_theorems_as_ovms.txt`)
against the table above:

- **Navier-Stokes** — its entire Clay statement sits on the criticality
  coordinate alone ("the entire transition is this single coordinate"). This
  is the tightest match to ⊙, the pinch itself.
- **Yang-Mills** — mass gap sits on completeness. Lands on λ_C, the split
  shell, not the pinch.
- **Collatz** — Dedekind-finiteness also sits on completeness. Shares λ_C
  with Yang-Mills.
- **BSD** — stoichiometry (|A|=1∧|B|=1) sits on composition. Lands at ∋ /
  the coupler.
- **Hodge** — long exact sequence sits on composition (shares ∋ with BSD);
  bidegree "return in two steps" sits on chirality, trine vertex 2.
- **Riemann** — functional equation stated as μ∘δ = id, the self-reference
  closure. Lands on trine vertex 3, ⊞.
- **P vs NP** — winding alone, an integer separation. Not a point feature;
  belongs to the knot's overall turn count.
- **Dynamics (trine vertex 1)** — uniform "static" across all seven. No
  single theorem owns it; it is the family's shared floor.

Note on instrument independence: this reading (pinch = Navier-Stokes,
completeness shell = Yang-Mills/Collatz) differs from `[[ym_horn_torus]]`,
which put Yang-Mills at the pinch under a different question (criticality as
abstract coordinate value, not this paper's named geometric feature). Two
instruments, two questions, two answers — hold both, do not collapse them.

## Open slots on the geometry, not yet assigned

- The A₂ equatorial triangle (n₊, n₋, n₋) in the top-down view — distinct
  from the evaluator trine, not yet matched to any theorem's coordinate.
- γ(0), the outer equator marker at x=2R — not yet tied to a mark.
- The involution/parity coordinate ≺, which carries half of Riemann's
  statement in the OVM paper, has no named home on this torus yet.

The V⊙x audit compiles the module's computable kernel to an ELF and lifts every

## 2. The three bugs found and fixed

### v1 → v3: closed constants defeat the lifted audit (native 7 → 20)
Lean's codegen constant-folds `if 16*16*16 = 4096 then 1 else 0` into a
`static uint8_t` closed constant, lazily initialized by
`initialize_HornTorusELF`. dlopen/ctypes never calls that initializer, so every
folded check read its static as 0 → native returned 7 of 20.
Fix (v3, runtime-only kernel): thread the audit input n into EVERY condition as
the runtime zero `n - n` (and bind the seven words as `word + z n`), so no
expression is closed. The codegen emits pure runtime branches — no statics, no
initializer, and every check is a real branch for V⊙x to pair.
The Python replica always gave 20/20 — the disagreement was compilation
semantics, not logic. Verdict: Lean semantics were right; the ELF contract was
wrong (uninitialized statics under ctypes). The v3 kernel documents the fix in
HornTorusELF.lean.

### PLT indirection halts the lifted run (vox run → "no instruction at 0x0")
The lifted horn_torus_check called the helpers (featureOf64, countDig16,
lengthOf, opAt) through the PLT. vox reads the RAW FILE bytes: the GOT
relocations that the dynamic linker fills at dlopen are zeros in the file, so
the PLT stub's `jmp *GOT` read 0 → pc = 0x0 → halt (after 285 steps, deep in
the first countDig16).
Fix: link with `-Wl,-Bsymbolic` (a bare `-Bsymbolic` is silently dropped by the
gcc driver — only the -Wl form reaches ld). All calls become direct in-image;
readelf shows FLAGS SYMBOLIC and zero `@plt` calls in horn_torus_check.
(`-fvisibility=hidden` was tried and rejected: it hides LEAN_EXPORT too.)

### V⊙x instrumentation (trace patch)
imasm_vm.rs call() now keeps a 12-entry ring of (pc, glyph, fields) and prints
"previous 12" in halt errors — what made the 0x0 halt diagnosable in one run.
Rebuilt at Vox/target/release/vox (patched binary also installed to
/home/mrnob0dy666/.cargo/bin/vox).

## 3. The runtime shim

HornTorusRuntime.c provides the seven lean_uint64 primitives the kernel
references (add, sub, land, shift_left, shift_right, dec_eq, dec_lt) so every
call target is in-image. The lifted image then executes the FULL computation —
primitives included — with no external resolution.

  fused back to depth zero is therefore exposed to the next reversal, while the
  same result held one level up survives it.
  So when a program COUNTS or ESTABLISHES something, then REVERSES direction
  (AREV), then BOUNDS or CONCLUDES: open the region that will HOLD the result
  BEFORE opening the region that COMPUTES it, and close them in that order.
    wrong: ... FSPLIT compute FFUSE  CLINK  FSPLIT AREV bound FFUSE ...
             the computed result is in the open when AREV arrives and is lost
    right: ... FSPLIT  FSPLIT compute FFUSE  CLINK AREV bound  FFUSE ...
             the inner FFUSE folds into the enclosing frame, AREV costs the
             register everything and the frame nothing, the outer FFUSE
             restores exactly what the clear took
  This is what a proof does when it establishes a lemma and keeps it in scope
  while a later chain runs: the lemma is the outer frame.

  A SECOND AND INDEPENDENT RULE. Whether anything is banked is the above.
  Whether a SURPLUS survives is a different question, decided by where the
  splits fall between deposits of the SAME value:
    two EVALT in ONE region      -> the region carries both, both come back
    two EVALT split by an FSPLIT -> sibling regions, the fold keeps the LARGER
  So a program can bank correctly and still lose a count, and a program can
  deposit carefully into one region and lose everything because its FFUSE ran
  before the reversal. Neither rule implies the other; both are proved in
  p4ramill Imscribing/IMASM/BankedWeight.lean.
  Explicit graph tools support cross-branch routing. This JSON schema carries
  a sequence only; imscr_wiring supplies its standard edges. It does not
  accept arbitrary cross-branch overrides.

EXPLICIT GRAPH COMPOSITION
  CLINK.o, IMSCRIB.o and IFIX.o may connect to compatible free inputs.
  A connection does not assign a register value by itself. The graph-flow
  evaluator computes that value from source seeds and the executed gates.
  This sequence-only schema cannot request arbitrary loop edges.

REGISTER STATE TRANSITIONS
  Sequential banked evaluator, carrier P({T,F,t,f}):
  VINIT clears register and frames. TANCH and CLINK preserve state.
  AFWD and IMSCRIB seed T only when the register is empty.
  AREV clears the register and retains open frames.
  EVALT deposits T; EVALF deposits F; ENGAGR deposits both t and f.
  FSPLIT opens an empty frame; FFUSE unions its deposits into the register
  and enclosing frame. IFIX freezes subsequent operations except IMSCRIB
  and repeated IFIX. Repeated IFIX does not create another mutable state.
  The graph-flow interpreter is a separate interpretation of explicit edges:
  AREV is the Lean involution, EVALT/EVALF are projections and IFIX carries.
  Diagram node observations of the sequential walk are not graph edge flow.

  FROBENIUS:  FSPLIT FFUSE
  DIALETHEIA: EVALT EVALF ENGAGR
  LINEAR:     IFIX

FREE COMPOSITION RULES
  1. Use as many tokens as the domain requires -- there is NO minimum or maximum length
  2. Expand token by token until every distinct operation, branch, state,
     and decision in the domain has been explicitly represented
  3. Each step: "OPCODE: what this token does at this point in the composition"
  4. Every FSPLIT must have exactly one matching FFUSE (stack-matched, innermost first).
     That stack rule is the WIRING convention: it says which arms get routed to which
     join when the sequence is built. It is NOT how closure is judged. A checker pairs
     by ANCESTRY over the edges -- two distinct in-arms of a FFUSE tracing back to a
     common FSPLIT, however they routed -- and where several FSPLIT qualify (an upstream
     fork reaches every later join on a strand) the join pairs with the INNERMOST one.
     The two agree on a plain strand, which is why the stack rule is a sound way to
     WRITE a sequence; they part company as soon as edges route otherwise (cross-branch,
     rule 6 below).
  5. EVALT anchors the T-branch; EVALF anchors the F-branch.
     AFWD (forward morphism) also anchors T-branch if EVALT is absent.
     AREV (parity flip / reverse morphism) also anchors F-branch if EVALF is absent.
  6. ENGAGR at any position enters B-state (paradice: both simultaneously held)
  7. IMSCRIB at both first and last position creates a self-referential closed loop
  8. Multiple FSPLIT/FFUSE pairs (sequential or nested) map multiple branch points
  9. Use IFIX as many times as needed -- each is a distinct permanent record event
  10. Do NOT compress -- if the domain has 30 distinct operations, write 30 tokens

WHY RULE 2 AND RULE 10 ARE SAFE (inflation invariance)
  Expanding costs nothing structural. A 1->1 token adds exactly one node and one edge,
  so the circuit rank beta = E - V + C cannot move, and the census (branch, merge,
  source, sink, arms) cannot move either. Extent grows without bound; structure does
  not. This is why "expand token by token" and "do NOT compress" are free instructions
  rather than a distortion of the domain: a longer faithful sequence is the SAME
  topology as a shorter one, never a different one.
  IMSCRIB (⊙) is the neutral element of that expansion: it is identity/self-reference
  and does NOT transform, so inserting it at any depth leaves the verdict untouched.
  The transforming tokens (> < ⋈ ⊤ ⊥ ⊞ ⊡) are NOT neutral -- a single one placed on an
  arm between FSPLIT and FFUSE turns an identity closure into a real one. So: expand
  freely to map the domain, but only put a transforming token on an arm when the domain
  really does work there.
  A token is irreducible in KIND but unbounded in EXTENT: any 1->2 replacement must
  itself contain a FSPLIT (it is the only brancher), so a fork reappears inside its own
  expansion. Same for FFUSE (2->1) and VINIT (0->1).


TOPOLOGICAL DIVERSITY
=====================
The IMASM composition rules explicitly permit nesting, open forks, and cross-branch routing.
DO NOT default to flat chains when the domain requires richer topology.

NESTING: FSPLIT/FFUSE pairs may nest. A branch can itself contain a sub-fork:
  FSPLIT EVALT [inner FSPLIT EVALT EVALF FFUSE] EVALF FFUSE
Use when the domain has hierarchical sub-decisions within a branch.

OPEN FORKS: A FSPLIT without a matching FFUSE creates a permanently divergent path.
Its unmatched output ports remain open; a later VINIT is a separate source.
Use when the domain has independent parallel processes that never recombine.

CROSS-BRANCH: arbitrary cross-branch edges require the explicit graph tools.
This sequence-only output schema uses imscr_wiring standard routing; do not claim
that prose descriptions add or override its edges.

EMPTY BRANCHES: FSPLIT immediately followed by FFUSE is valid (vacuous evaluation).
Use when the structural form matters more than a particular branch's content.

DECISION VS ITERATION: FSPLIT models a genuine either/or, two arms that could each be
taken because the domain actually forks on a choice. Building n similar items in
sequence (n cliques, n rounds of one process, n members of a family) is not a decision
and takes a CLINK chain, one CLINK per item, never an FSPLIT, even when n is a variable
and even when there are many of them. A fork earns its FFUSE by putting genuinely
different content on each arm. An empty arm is permitted. Structural closure needs a transformed reconnection.
The insert-repair banked-clear observation asks whether a clear had protected
weight; its vacuity result does not decide graph reconnection or arm work.

Choose the topology that best fits the domain. Flat chains are ONE option, not the default.

# Horn Torus Geometry — Context Sheet

Source: `manuscripts3/sic_moduli_conductor.tex`, section "The Geometric
Realization: The Horn Torus and (16,3) Knot," plus the cross-reference against
`millennium_theorems_as_ovms.txt` worked out 2026-08-23.

## The object

A horn torus is the degenerate torus where tube radius equals centre radius,
R = r. The hole closes to a single point instead of staying open. That point
is the pinch, marked ⊙. It is not a drawing artifact — it is the condition
that lets the surface touch itself, the geometric picture of self-reference.

Two lobes, each of radius R, centred at x = ±R on the syzygy axis, tangent at
the origin. The tangency point is ⊙.

## The named features and their coordinates

Side-on section (xz-plane, y=0), the frame the paper actually draws in:

- **⊙ (pinch).** Origin. Where the two lobes touch.
- **λ_C (the split shell).** Dashed circle centred on ⊙, radius r = R/2. This
  is the ∈ split — the completeness coordinate given a located geometric
  home.
- **Evaluator sphere.** Same radius r as λ_C, centred one radius along the
  axis from ⊙. Passes through both ⊙ and ∋.
- **∋.** At x = 2. The far point the evaluator sphere reaches.
- **Coupler.** The heavy segment between ⊙ and ∋ — the line the evaluator
  sphere's passage traces out.
- **Evaluator trine.** ⊤, ⊥, ⊞ at x = 1, z = 0, ±√3/2 in this section —
  collinear here because the section is edge-on to it. In the axial view
  (looking down the syzygy axis) the trine is face-on: an equilateral
  triangle at 120° on a circle. Exact coordinates, confirmed against
  `WINDING/massive_winding/winding_reformulation/k3v_geometry/evaluator_sphere/evaluator_sphere_analysis.md`:
  EVALT (λ_C, λ_C, 0), EVALF (λ_C, −λ_C/2, λ_C√3/2), ENGAGR ⊞ (λ_C, −λ_C/2,
  −λ_C√3/2) — all three on the evaluator sphere's equatorial circle at
  x = λ_C, by construction. **ENGAGR (⊞) also sits on the horn torus surface
  itself** — not in the same untilted frame the evaluator sphere is drawn
  in, but under the tilt that reconciles the two: the evaluator frame (3
  arms on the Compton/evaluator sphere) and the 16-sector grid (the (16,3)
  knot on the horn torus) are related by a rotation of arctan(1/4) around
  the syzygy axis, a 7.5° sector offset (`k3v_geometry/parametric_arm/parametric_arm_analysis.md`
  §5.2). A same-frame membership check against the untilted torus equation
  will show ENGAGR off the surface — that checks the wrong frame, not the
  wrong claim.
- **γ(0), outer equator.** Marker at x = 2R.
- **γ(π), the horn.** The pinch itself, where the equatorial curve
  degenerates — same point as ⊙, named from the curve's parametrization
  rather than the tangency.

Top-down section (z=0): the same λ_C and evaluator-sphere circles side by
side, ∋ at x=2, and the three 120°-equator points are the A₂ roots (one n₊
against two n₋) — their triangle is the knot's poloidal winding read as a
circuit. This equatorial A₂ triangle is **not** the evaluator trine; the
trine collapses to the short edge-on segment at x=1 in this view. Two
different triangles, both real, do not conflate them.

Axial section (looking down the syzygy axis): the outline is unchanged
(horn is symmetric about this axis), but ⊙, the coupler, and ∋, which were
spread out in the other two views, now stack on the axis with ⊙ nearest.
λ_C and the evaluator sphere become one circle (concentric, equal radius).
The trine, edge-on everywhere else, is face-on here — this is the view
where ⊤, ⊥, ⊞ actually show as the equilateral triangle at 120°.

## The (16,3) knot

Sixteen toroidal windings against three poloidal ones, traced by the
evaluator arms. Bridge number three matches the three arms carrying the
four-valued kernel. Sixteen matches the trilattice's state count (2⁴ = 16,
also |I|² = 16 — the two coincide only at n=4, Proposition 2.3 in the
paper). This pair (16,3) is also the conductor exponent structure at
d=2048: 𝔣 = (2¹²)∞₁ = (16³)∞₁.

## Mark-to-feature table

| Feature | Mark(s) | Named role |
|---|---|---|
| Pinch ⊙ | ⊙ (criticality) | Tangency; hole closes to a point |
| Split shell λ_C | ∈ (completeness) | Radius r = R/2, centred on the pinch |
| Evaluator sphere / coupler / ∋ | ∋ (composition) | Passes through ⊙ and ∋, radius r |
| Trine, vertex 1 | ⊤ (dynamics) | Static for all seven Clay theorems alike — not a differentiator |
| Trine, vertex 2 | ⊥ (chirality) | "Return in exactly two steps" |
| Trine, vertex 3 | ⊞ (self-reference) | μ∘δ = id closure; on the evaluator sphere AND the horn torus surface (via the arctan(1/4) tilt) — the only trine member confirmed on both |
| Knot winding overall | ⊡ (winding) | Not a point — the toroidal count itself, 16 turns |
| Involution / parity | ≺ | Not pictured as a torus feature in this paper |

## Cross-reference to the seven Clay theorems

Reading each theorem's OVM-coordinate word (`millennium_theorems_as_ovms.txt`)
against the table above:

- **Navier-Stokes** — its entire Clay statement sits on the criticality
  coordinate alone ("the entire transition is this single coordinate"). This
  is the tightest match to ⊙, the pinch itself.
- **Yang-Mills** — mass gap sits on completeness. Lands on λ_C, the split
  shell, not the pinch.
- **Collatz** — Dedekind-finiteness also sits on completeness. Shares λ_C
  with Yang-Mills.
- **BSD** — stoichiometry (|A|=1∧|B|=1) sits on composition. Lands at ∋ /
  the coupler.
- **Hodge** — long exact sequence sits on composition (shares ∋ with BSD);
  bidegree "return in two steps" sits on chirality, trine vertex 2.
- **Riemann** — functional equation stated as μ∘δ = id, the self-reference
  closure. Lands on trine vertex 3, ⊞.
- **P vs NP** — winding alone, an integer separation. Not a point feature;
  belongs to the knot's overall turn count.
- **Dynamics (trine vertex 1)** — uniform "static" across all seven. No
  single theorem owns it; it is the family's shared floor.

Note on instrument independence: this reading (pinch = Navier-Stokes,
completeness shell = Yang-Mills/Collatz) differs from `[[ym_horn_torus]]`,
which put Yang-Mills at the pinch under a different question (criticality as
abstract coordinate value, not this paper's named geometric feature). Two
instruments, two questions, two answers — hold both, do not collapse them.

## Open slots on the geometry, not yet assigned

- The A₂ equatorial triangle (n₊, n₋, n₋) in the top-down view — distinct
  from the evaluator trine, not yet matched to any theorem's coordinate.
- γ(0), the outer equator marker at x=2R — not yet tied to a mark.
- The involution/parity coordinate ≺, which carries half of Riemann's
  statement in the OVM paper, has no named home on this torus yet.

## 1. What was audited

The V⊙x audit compiles the module's computable kernel to an ELF and lifts every

## 2. The three bugs found and fixed

### v1 → v3: closed constants defeat the lifted audit (native 7 → 20)
Lean's codegen constant-folds `if 16*16*16 = 4096 then 1 else 0` into a
`static uint8_t` closed constant, lazily initialized by
`initialize_HornTorusELF`. dlopen/ctypes never calls that initializer, so every
folded check read its static as 0 → native returned 7 of 20.
Fix (v3, runtime-only kernel): thread the audit input n into EVERY condition as
the runtime zero `n - n` (and bind the seven words as `word + z n`), so no
expression is closed. The codegen emits pure runtime branches — no statics, no
initializer, and every check is a real branch for V⊙x to pair.
The Python replica always gave 20/20 — the disagreement was compilation
semantics, not logic. Verdict: Lean semantics were right; the ELF contract was
wrong (uninitialized statics under ctypes). The v3 kernel documents the fix in
HornTorusELF.lean.

### PLT indirection halts the lifted run (vox run → "no instruction at 0x0")
The lifted horn_torus_check called the helpers (featureOf64, countDig16,
lengthOf, opAt) through the PLT. vox reads the RAW FILE bytes: the GOT
relocations that the dynamic linker fills at dlopen are zeros in the file, so
the PLT stub's `jmp *GOT` read 0 → pc = 0x0 → halt (after 285 steps, deep in
the first countDig16).
Fix: link with `-Wl,-Bsymbolic` (a bare `-Bsymbolic` is silently dropped by the
gcc driver — only the -Wl form reaches ld). All calls become direct in-image;
readelf shows FLAGS SYMBOLIC and zero `@plt` calls in horn_torus_check.
(`-fvisibility=hidden` was tried and rejected: it hides LEAN_EXPORT too.)

### V⊙x instrumentation (trace patch)
imasm_vm.rs call() now keeps a 12-entry ring of (pc, glyph, fields) and prints
"previous 12" in halt errors — what made the 0x0 halt diagnosable in one run.
Rebuilt at Vox/target/release/vox (patched binary also installed to
/home/mrnob0dy666/.cargo/bin/vox).

## 3. The runtime shim

HornTorusRuntime.c provides the seven lean_uint64 primitives the kernel
references (add, sub, land, shift_left, shift_right, dec_eq, dec_lt) so every
call target is in-image. The lifted image then executes the FULL computation —
primitives included — with no external resolution.
